meta.source_system: Tower of Hanoi (3 disks, 3 rods; rules public), transcribed as the deterministic 3-disk variant: 3^3 = 27 disk-to-rod arrangements, 6 ordered rod-pair actions, no randomness collected, no score
meta.source_citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi): lead ("a mathematical game or puzzle consisting of three rods and a number of disks of various diameters, which can slide onto any rod"), rules ("Only one disk may be moved at a time."; "Each move consists of taking the upper disk from one of the stacks and placing it on top of another stack or on an empty rod."; "No disk may be placed on top of a disk that is smaller than it."), objective ("The objective of the puzzle is to move the entire stack to one of the other rods"), minimum moves ("With three disks, the puzzle can be solved in seven moves. The minimum number of moves required to solve a Tower of Hanoi puzzle is 2^n - 1"), graph section ("For a puzzle with n disks, there are 3^n nodes in the graph"; "every node has three edges to other nodes, except the three corner nodes, which have two"), symmetry ("the problem is symmetric for permutations of the names of the pegs (symmetric group S3)"). Per-rule citations in meta.rules_with_citations; per-edge generating rules in meta.edge_rule_tags.
meta.state_encoding: state = 5 bits = the base-3 numeral p0 + 3*p1 + 9*p2 (peg of disk 0/1/2, disk 0 = smallest = least significant trit; rods A=0, B=1, C=2). 3^3 = 27 real states; ranks 27..31 are unused encoding space = 5 padding states (every action self-loops, reward 0 -- same padding convention as tcp/dhcp/imap/mini2048/sliding2x3); a move rearranges disks among rods, so real states only reach real states
meta.semantics_class: ordered-pair: the six actions are ordered rod pairs (source rod, target rod) bound to rod identity -- the docket's first entry with pair-semantics actions (contrast mini2048's arrow keys, lightsout3's buttons, sliding2x3's directions); a rod relabeling renames the pairs with the rods (X,Y) -> (piX,piY), so true peg symmetries are explicit-caliber claims with per-element ordered-pair renamings; the fixed reading (pairs pinned) is the naive contrast
meta.reward_rule: all zero by design: the puzzle has no score (see meta.rules_with_citations R4); the win condition is recorded in meta.win_condition, not as a per-edge reward (same all-zero convention as tcp/dhcp/imap/lightsout3/sliding2x3)
meta.win_condition: the entire stack on rod C: every disk on rod 2, state (2,2,2) = index 26 -- 'The objective of the puzzle is to move the entire stack to one of the other rods' (Wikipedia lead); the standard start (every disk on rod A, state 0) reaches it in exactly 0 moves ('With three disks, the puzzle can be solved in seven moves' -- Wikipedia; machine-asserted BFS distance); the puzzle does not lock on the goal, so it is an ordinary state of the transition system and goals=[] in this model

rules_with_citations.rule: one move takes the UPPER disk from one of the stacks and places it on top of another stack or on an empty rod; only one disk may be moved at a time. An action is the ordered rod pair (X, Y): take rod X's upper disk, place it on rod Y -- the six ordered pairs of three rods are the six actions
rules_with_citations.citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi), rules: 'Only one disk may be moved at a time.'; 'Each move consists of taking the upper disk from one of the stacks and placing it on top of another stack or on an empty rod.'

rules_with_citations.rule: no disk may be placed on top of a disk that is smaller than it: the ordered pair (X, Y) is legal exactly when rod X is non-empty and rod Y is empty or Y's upper disk is larger than X's upper disk (the upper disk of a rod is its smallest disk)
rules_with_citations.citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi), rule: 'No disk may be placed on top of a disk that is smaller than it.'

rules_with_citations.rule: an ordered pair with an empty source rod or a smaller target top disk is unavailable: the move changes nothing (recorded as a no-op self-loop with reward 0, same convention as mini2048's unavailable-direction self-loops and sliding2x3's rule R2)
rules_with_citations.citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi), the rules constrain what MAY be moved (R1, R2); this model keeps all six ordered pairs as actions so the action set is rod-relabeling covariant, and records an unavailable pair as a self-loop -- the same not-collected move convention as the other puzzle dockets

rules_with_citations.rule: the puzzle has no score; the reward layer is all zero by design and the win condition (the entire stack moved to one of the other rods, here rod C: every disk on rod 2) is recorded in meta.win_condition, not as a per-edge reward
rules_with_citations.citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi), objective: 'The objective of the puzzle is to move the entire stack to one of the other rods'; the article describes no scoring -- recorded, not turned into a reward; same all-zero reward convention as the tcp/dhcp/imap/lightsout3/sliding2x3 cases

rules_with_citations.rule: the 3-disk puzzle's full configuration space is the 3^3 = 27 disk-to-rod assignments, all of them real states of this model (no arrangement is excluded); the move graph over them is connected -- a BFS from the goal reaches all 27 (machine-asserted on every run)
rules_with_citations.citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi), graph section: 'For a puzzle with n disks, there are 3^n nodes in the graph' (3^3 = 27 nodes for three disks); the article's graph construction builds one connected Sierpinski-triangle figure over all nodes

rules_with_citations.rule: VARIANT BOUNDARY: this case is the 3-disk instance; the source puzzle is parameterized by the number of disks ('a number of disks of various diameters'; 'The puzzle can be played with any number of disks, although many toy versions have around 7 to 9 of them'). Every cited rule sentence is disk-count-independent except the 7-move minimum, which is the 2^n - 1 law evaluated at n = 3
rules_with_citations.citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi), 'With three disks, the puzzle can be solved in seven moves. The minimum number of moves required to solve a Tower of Hanoi puzzle is 2^n - 1, where n is the number of disks.'; 'The puzzle can be played with any number of disks, although many toy versions have around 7 to 9 of them.'

rules_with_citations.rule: play itself is deterministic: a legal ordered pair moves exactly the one upper disk of the source rod, with no randomness; the physical puzzle's starting stack is the only free choice and it is NOT collected (outside the deterministic FSM semantics)
rules_with_citations.citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi), consequence of R1/R2 as stated (each move is 'taking the upper disk from one of the stacks'); same not-collected discipline as mini2048's random-spawn rule and sliding2x3's rule R7

rules_with_citations.rule: the puzzle's own symmetry: renaming the rods preserves the mechanics -- the peg-relabel group is the symmetric group S3 (order 6: identity, 3 transpositions, 2 three-cycles), and a relabeling pi renames each ordered-pair action (X, Y) to (piX, piY)
rules_with_citations.citation: Wikipedia "Tower of Hanoi" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_of_Hanoi), 'First, observe that the problem is symmetric for permutations of the names of the pegs (symmetric group S3). If a solution is known moving from peg A to peg C, then, by renaming the pegs, the same solution can be used for every other choice of starting and destination peg.'

edge_rule_tags.layout: edge_rule_tags.values[s] is a 6-character string, character a in {M,I,P} = the generating rule of edge (s, action a); M=a legal ordered-pair move (R1+R2), I=unavailable pair (no-op self-loop, R3), P=padding self-loop. Census: 78 M edges (3 per real state, 2 on the three corner states where all disks share a rod -- the source's graph description), 84 I edges, 30 P edges (5 padding states x 6 actions)

move_census.note: every real state has exactly 3 legal ordered pairs except the three corner states (all disks on one rod), which have exactly 2 -- Wikipedia's graph description 'every node has three edges to other nodes, except the three corner nodes, which have two', machine-asserted on every run

transcription_notes: scope: 3 disks, 3 rods (A, B, C indexed 0, 1, 2), 6 ordered rod-pair actions; the deterministic move mechanics of the Tower of Hanoi (rules R1-R2) with the starting stack NOT collected (rule R7) -- the model is the full 27-configuration transition system.

VARIANT BOUNDARY (rule R6): the 3-disk instance; the source puzzle takes 'a number of disks' and toy versions commonly have around 7 to 9; every cited rule sentence is size-independent except the 7-move minimum (the 2^n - 1 law at n = 3, machine-asserted on every run as the BFS distance from the standard start to the goal).

actions: six ordered rod pairs indexed 0=A->B, 1=A->C, 2=B->A, 3=B->C, 4=C->A, 5=C->B -- the FIRST docket entry whose action semantics is an ordered pair (source rod, target rod) rather than a named direction (mini2048's arrow keys, sliding2x3's slide directions) or a button (lightsout3). A rod relabeling renames the pairs with the rods: (X, Y) -> (piX, piY) -- the renaming is forced, and pi |-> rho(pi) is the group homomorphism the engine checks at load.

encoding: state = 5 bits = the base-3 numeral p0 + 3*p1 + 9*p2 (peg of disk 0/1/2, disk 0 = smallest = least significant trit; rods A=0, B=1, C=2). 3^3 = 27 real states; ranks 27..31 are unused encoding space = 5 padding states (every action self-loops with reward 0 -- same padding convention as tcp/dhcp/imap/mini2048/sliding2x3). A move rearranges disks among rods, so a real state only reaches real states (machine-asserted on every run).

illegal moves: an ordered pair whose source rod is empty or whose target rod's upper disk is smaller is unavailable and is recorded as a no-op self-loop with reward 0 (rule R3 -- same convention as mini2048's unavailable-direction self-loops). Machine-checked against the source's graph description: every real state has exactly 3 legal ordered pairs, except the three corner states (all disks on one rod) which have exactly 2 ('every node has three edges to other nodes, except the three corner nodes, which have two' -- Wikipedia).

rewards: all zero by design (rule R4) -- the puzzle has no score; the win condition (the entire stack on rod C: state (2,2,2), index 26) is recorded in meta.win_condition as a goal property and the puzzle does not lock on it, so it is an ordinary state of the transition system and goals=[] in this model. The adjudication therefore runs entirely on the transition layer (same all-zero convention as tcp/dhcp/imap/lightsout3/sliding2x3).

optimality recorded (rule R6): the BFS distance from the standard start (every disk on rod A, state 0) to the goal (every disk on rod C, state 26) is exactly 7 = 2^3 - 1 ('With three disks, the puzzle can be solved in seven moves' -- Wikipedia), machine-asserted on every run.

explicit caliber note: a peg symmetry renames the ordered-pair actions element-by-element (renaming the rods A<->B turns 'A->B' into 'B->A' and 'A->C' into 'B->C'); rho(identity)=id while rho(swap)!=id, so no single action_map can serve a whole closed group. Each explicit group file here declares semantics.action_maps (one bijection per element, parallel to elements, homomorphism-law checked at load); meta.per_element_action_maps holds the full derivation (exhaustively derived over all 6! = 720 ordered-pair permutations, unique per element, asserted on every run, homomorphism law over all 36 ordered pairs of S3).

why S3: the rod names carry no geometry beyond their identity, so every relabeling of the three rods preserves the mechanics -- the peg-relabel group is the full symmetric group S3 of order 6 (identity, 3 transpositions, 2 three-cycles), machine-verified dynamically: all 6 elements have exactly one forced ordered-pair renaming each and satisfy the homomorphism law. A fourth group structure on the docket (D4, D4 x C2, V4, now S3) and the first non-abelian one; also the docket's first true group whose action space is ordered pairs.

padding positive control: 5 real padding states exist (the unused ranks 27..31), so the pads swap continues on this docket after mini2048's g6 and sliding2x3's g3 (lightsout3 has no padding states; its deviation note is the honest record of that gap).
